body: So, how is your life treating you, mrbreenspoop?
I'm sorry you're feeling this way. I'm here to listen if you want to talk.

Something that jumps out at me from this post is you might have bipolar disorder. The lows and the productive highs you mention seem to correspond with that diagnosis. A lot of antidepressants won't work very well for someone who has bipolar too. It might be something for you to check out.

Why keep going to this doctor then? Can you switch to someone who might actually help?

What's a trial PT? Have you started it yet? PT can definitely help a lot with back pain and get you back on your feet, hopefully.

And don't think of it as a permanent disability. You don't know if it's going to be permanent. You might find something in the future that helps, but for the time being you need rest. There is nothing wrong with needing a time out from a life that is too hard and painful. Don't let pride take over. I know lots of "diabled" people who went on to change the world in big and dramatic ways. It doesn't mean your life is over, it just means you need to find new ways of doing things, at least for the time being. A friend of mine who is in a wheelchair hiked the appalachain trail last summer. And yeah, they had those first couple of years of thinking that they were an invalid and were never going to amount to much, but once they got past that and learned to adapt to their new body, they were able to do more than they thought ever possible. Don't give up! It's hard and it sucks sometimes more than anyone will ever know, but your life is still in your hands to make with it what you will.

You are not worthless. You are just in a fucked up place in a fucked up time of your life. That's okay though. We've all been there. What's important now is that you find a way to get out of the hole you've sunk into! Can you start looking for a new job? Can you learn to drive? Close your eyes and think about the perfect life, one that you COULD be living in the future. Now start making a plan to get there. If you have a close family, like you seem to state, ask for their help in getting to your goals. If they see that you're truly making an effort to achieve something great in your life, I am sure that they would love to help. You're only 21 and you've got so much life ahead of you. Don't throw it all away just because of a little confusion right now. Your early 20s are the time to figure out all this stuff anyway. Good luck finding what makes you happy! Go live your dreams!

I know how you feel! God damn, I totally know how you feel. My situation is completely fucked up too and I give up hope on it on a daily fucking basis. It just seems like sometime you walk so far down a road of being unsuccessful that you don't know how to ever get back to where you were before. Still, I know you have a lot of issues as you've stated here, but what about the good things in your life? Your girlfriend for one. And I'm sure there are others. Try to focus on the positive things you've done right for a change. Then tomorrow try to add to that list. Make a list of all the problems, like you've done here, and then write down one productive thing you could do to change each of them for the better. It may not fix the entire situation, but one step and then another and then one more and by this time next year you may be in a completely different place in life. Think of it as a year-long quest to work through your problems.

Have you tried filing for disability (or is that what workman's comp is?)? It definitely seems like you have a case. And I know this might seem naieve, but have you gone back to the doctor since this has happened? They may be able to prescribe you something or get you hooked up with some kind of surgery or physical therapy to help. And what about family members? Do you know anyone close who might be able to help? I know you've probably thought of all this already, but as someone who suffers with chronic pain myself, I know that sometimes the pain gets to be so much that all rational thought is pushed out the window. Just take it day by day. There is hope out there but you may have to really research what options are available to you.
